title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: A great balance sheet lets an exchange survive a decade of regulatory transition and emerge with zero debt and 71% returns on capital.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: MCX's ten-year financial record (FY15–FY26, plus Sep 2026 / TTM) is one of the cleanest operating-leverage stories in Indian finance [1]. From FY15 to FY22, sales crept from ₹222 crore to ₹367 crore. Operating margins stayed boxed at 29% to 47% due to legacy software fees [1][16]. In FY23 and FY24, emergency extension fees to 63 Moons—peaking at ₹125 crore/quarter in H2 CY23—pushed total costs to ₹621 crore in FY24 [1][15]. That squeezed FY24 OPM to 9% and PAT to ₹83 crore [1]. Once the TCS platform went live in October 2023, expenses fell to ₹447 crore in FY25 and ₹660 crore in FY26 [1]. Meanwhile, sales surged to ₹1,113 crore (FY25), ₹2,302 crore (FY26), and ₹3,056 crore (TTM Sep 2026), lifting OPM to 60%, 71%, and 74% TTM [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26 & TTM Sep 2026) [1]

web_blocks.html: Two P&L items merit a closer look. First, depreciation rose from ₹22 crore in FY23 to ₹36 crore in FY24, ₹64 crore in FY25, and ₹78 crore in FY26 (₹84 crore TTM) [1]. Capitalized TCS platform spend moved out of Capital Work-in-Progress into Fixed Assets [1]. CWIP peaked at ₹169 crore in FY23 and fell to ₹16 crore in FY24 [1]. Fixed Assets rose from ₹150 crore in FY23 to ₹379 crore in FY24 and ₹479 crore by Sep 2026 [1]. Second, Other Income—interest on own reserves and clearing float—grew from ₹75 crore in FY24 to ₹98 crore in FY25, ₹127 crore in FY26, and ₹170 crore TTM [1][10]. That float income provides a steady profit floor even in quiet trading months [1][10].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26 & Sep 2026) [1]

web_blocks.html: The balance sheet is a fortress. MCX holds almost zero debt: ₹5 crore in Mar 2026 and ₹9 crore in Sep 2026, against ₹3,512 crore of net worth [1]. Net worth comprises ₹51 crore Equity Capital and ₹3,461 crore Reserves [1]. Cash and investments grew from ₹914 crore in FY24 to ₹2,949 crore in FY26 and ₹3,106 crore by Sep 2026 [1]. Watch the paired jump in Other Liabilities (₹2,029 crore in FY24 to ₹4,648 crore in FY26 and ₹4,266 crore in Sep 2026) and Other Assets (₹2,100 crore to ₹4,180 crore) [1][13]. Those lines reflect clearing member margin deposits and settlement funds held at MCXCCL, alongside the ₹1,367.29 crore Core SGF pool [1][13]. Management also noted in H1 FY27 that SEBI's Z-score tweaks eased mandatory SGF top-up needs, reducing near-term cash lockup [13].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26) [1]

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion is strong. In FY26, MCX posted ₹3,035 crore in Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) against ₹1,332 crore of PAT (228% CFO/PAT, or 202% CFO/EBITDA) [1]. Tiny capex of ₹73 crore left ₹2,962 crore in Free Cash Flow [1]. About ₹1,700 crore of FY26 CFO came from clearing margin float inflows, mirrored in Investing Cash Flow of -₹2,399 crore as MCXCCL parked collateral in liquid funds [1]. Even without float swings, core FCF converts at ~100% of PAT [1]. That cash supports a 27%–65% historical dividend payout while compounding ROCE to 71.4% and ROE to 56.3% [1].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Cleanliness Verdict
paragraphs: Debtor days stay tight at 10 days, down from 33 days in the FY24 transition year [1]. Working capital sits at -465 days due to upfront margin collection, and ROCE jumped from 7% in FY24 to 43% in FY25 and 71% in FY26 [1].

MCX carries no debt overhang and no equity dilution, with Equity Capital flat at ₹51 crore for over a decade [1]. There is also no aggressive capitalization, as CWIP fell back to ₹23 crore by Sep 2026 [1].

book_paragraphs: When you and I open MCX's ten-year financial statements, the first thing that jumps off the page is how boring the balance sheet is—and in financial infrastructure, boring is beautiful. Equity capital has sat unchanged at ₹51 crore for over a decade. Borrowings are essentially zero—just ₹9 crore in September 2026 against ₹3,512 crore of net worth and ₹3,106 crore of investments. Debtor days are just 10 days, working capital is negative 465 days, and Return on Capital Employed has vaulted from 7% during the FY24 software-transition trough to 43% in FY25 and 71.4% in FY26.

The forensic key to reading MCX's P&L is understanding the shift in how technology shows up in the accounts. Until October 2023, software was a massive variable operating expense paid to 63 Moons—peaking at ₹621 crore of total operating expenses in FY24. After migrating to TCS, MCX capitalized the new platform onto its balance sheet (lifting Fixed Assets from ₹150 crore in FY23 to ₹479 crore by September 2026) and now runs a predictable ₹105 crore annual IT bill plus ₹78 crore of annual depreciation. Because that cost base is largely fixed, every incremental crore of options turnover drops straight to operating profit, lifting margins from 9% in FY24 to 71% in FY26 and 74% on a trailing twelve-month basis.

Let's also check cash flow integrity. In FY26, MCX reported ₹3,035 crore of operating cash flow on ₹1,332 crore of net profit, with just ₹73 crore of capital expenditure. As we noted earlier, part of that cash surge comes from clearing member margin deposits sitting on MCXCCL's balance sheet, which you can see mirrored in the ₹2,399 crore of investing outflows into liquid instruments. Even without a single rupee of margin float, MCX's core business converts roughly 100% of its net profit into free cash flow—funded by zero leverage and protected by a ₹1,367 crore Settlement Guarantee Fund.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Reading an Exchange Balance Sheet Correctly
book_callouts.text: Never panic when you see 'Other Liabilities' jump from ₹2,029 crore to ₹4,648 crore on an exchange's balance sheet. Those are not borrowings; they are clearing member margin deposits held by MCXCCL, matched rupee-for-rupee by liquid investments and bank balances on the asset side.

book_subsections.title: The Ten-Year Arc: From Stagnant Tollbooth to Operating-Leverage Engine
paragraphs: MCX's ten-year consolidated P&L from FY15 through FY26 and trailing twelve months (Sep 2026) reads like a textbook study in cost-structure transformation. Between FY15 and FY22, operating revenue grew modestly from ₹222 crore to ₹367 crore (dipping briefly in FY21–FY22 after a ₹398 crore Covid-volatility peak in FY20), while operating margins stayed trapped between 29% and 47% under the weight of legacy software fees. Then came the FY23–FY24 migration crunch: emergency extension payouts to 63 Moons pushed operating expenses from ₹206 crore in FY22 to ₹369 crore in FY23 and ₹621 crore in FY24, crushing operating profit margin to 9% (₹63 crore on ₹684 crore of sales) and net profit to ₹83 crore.

Once the TCS Commodity Derivatives Platform went live in October 2023, that expense spike vanished. Total operating expenses fell to ₹447 crore in FY25 and rose only modestly to ₹660 crore in FY26 even as operating revenue surged to ₹1,113 crore in FY25, ₹2,302 crore in FY26, and ₹3,056 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Operating profit jumped from ₹63 crore (FY24) to ₹665 crore (FY25, 60% OPM), ₹1,642 crore (FY26, 71% OPM), and ₹2,263 crore TTM (74% OPM), driving net profit to ₹560 crore (FY25), ₹1,332 crore (FY26), and ₹1,799 crore TTM.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: CWIP, Margin Float & Zero Leverage
paragraphs: Two accounting details on the P&L and balance sheet deserve your close attention. First, depreciation stepped up from ₹22 crore in FY23 to ₹36 crore in FY24, ₹64 crore in FY25, ₹78 crore in FY26, and ₹84 crore TTM as capitalized TCS platform development moved out of Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP peaked at ₹169 crore in FY23, dropped to ₹16 crore in FY24, and stood at ₹23 crore in Sep 2026) onto Fixed Assets (rising from ₹150 crore in FY23 to ₹379 crore in FY24 and ₹479 crore by Sep 2026). There is no aggressive capitalization hiding ongoing expenses—the platform is live and depreciating cleanly.

Second, do not misread the surge in Other Liabilities (from ₹2,029 crore in FY24 to ₹4,648 crore in FY26 and ₹4,266 crore in Sep 2026) and Other Assets (₹2,100 crore to ₹4,180 crore). Those are not debt; MCX carries virtually zero borrowings (₹5 crore in Mar 2026, ₹9 crore in Sep 2026 against ₹3,512 crore of net worth and ₹3,106 crore of investments and cash). Instead, those balances represent clearing member margin deposits and settlement funds held by MCXCCL alongside the ₹1,367.29 crore Core SGF—and management noted in H1 FY27 that SEBI's Z-score adjustments moderated mandatory SGF top-up requirements, easing near-term cash retention.

book_subsections.title: Cash Conversion, Dividend Discipline & Return on Capital
paragraphs: Looking across the ten-year cash flow statement, you can also see why single-year CFO swings on an exchange must be interpreted carefully. In FY17 (-₹32 crore CFO) and FY21 (-₹184 crore CFO), collateral outflows temporarily depressed operating cash flow, whereas in FY26 booming trading activity brought roughly ₹1,700 crore of clearing margin float inflows—lifting CFO to ₹3,035 crore (202% CFO/EBITDA and 228% of ₹1,332 crore PAT), mirrored by -₹2,399 crore of investing cash flow as MCXCCL parked collateral in liquid instruments. With just ₹73 crore of capex, FY26 Free Cash Flow reached ₹2,962 crore. Strip out margin float, and core FCF still converts at ~100% of PAT. Meanwhile, equity capital has remained unchanged at ₹51 crore for over a decade with zero dilution, debtor days sit at 10 days (down from 33 days in FY24), working capital is -465 days, historical dividend payouts have ranged from 27% to 65% (15% in FY26 as reserves compounded), and ROCE has climbed from 7% in FY24 to 43% in FY25 and 71.4% in FY26 alongside 56.3% ROE.
